expectations.text: The feedback stops at the first structural failure; it does NOT deliver a full audit covering all four Parts of the checklist
expectations.evidence: The feedback names Part 4 as '第一个也是唯一要动的结构问题'. Part 1 (Normal) and the disturbance (Part 2) appear only inside the '先说做对的地方' positive section, not as an audit; Part 3 (Stakes) is never surfaced to the reader as a separate graded item. Only one structural failure (Part 4, the door) is delivered, matching the stop-at-first-failure format.

expectations.text: The feedback contains no item-by-item scoring table and does not output or fill in the self-check card
expectations.evidence: feedback.md is prose only — a one-line judgment, one positive block, one structural-failure block, one rewrite, one caveat. There is no Part-by-Part score table and no self-check card is emitted or filled in.

expectations.text: The feedback identifies the final sentence of the closing (containing 「感谢有你的关注」/「比大雨更持久，比虫鸣更让我开心」) as conclusion + named-emotion, i.e. an explanation-mode leak (4.2 / S.1)
expectations.evidence: Feedback quotes '但我能确定的是，你还在听我念叨。感谢有你的关注——这种感觉比大雨更持久，比虫鸣更让我开心。' and calls it 'skill 里说的 fail signal：结尾在"告诉"读者该有什么感受（"更持久""更让我开心"）……悬念被自己的结论盖掉了' — precisely conclusion + told/named feeling (explanation-mode leak).

expectations.text: The proposed fix is deletion-first and minimal, and it preserves the author's pivot line 「但我能确定的是，你还在听我念叨」 (or explicitly recommends it as the landing line)
expectations.evidence: Fix is a minimal reorder/deletion: '把最后一段的顺序倒过来，让感知落在最后' and '让文章停在那个分不清的声音上'. The rewrite preserves the pivot's content by moving it up front: '感谢你还在听我念叨。' The '你还在听我念叨' line is explicitly retained ('保留了你想表达的暖意（"你还在听我念叨"提前说掉）').

expectations.text: The feedback does NOT accuse the pivot 「但我能确定的是」 of violating 4.1 — using the disturbance as contrast/turn is not the same as explaining the disturbance itself, since the sound remains unidentified
expectations.evidence: The feedback never charges the pivot with a Part-4.1 disturbance-explanation violation. On the contrary it praises the sound as an unexplained disturbance: '"分不清是蛙还是虫"是一个漂亮的、被感知到的事实级扰动……它是具体的、未解释的、真实的。' The fault is placed only on the told-feeling final clause, not on 「但我能确定的是」 as a contrast turn.

expectations.text: The feedback recognizes the piece is a newsletter rather than a fiction scene, and does NOT ask the author to add a suspense-style disturbance or rewrite the close to hook-standard
expectations.evidence: '一个提醒：这是电子报不是小说章节，结尾"安顿读者"本身没错，不必每期都做成悬念钩子……所以这条你可以只当一个选项.' No demand to add a suspense disturbance or hit hook-standard; the change is explicitly optional.

expectations.text: The feedback does NOT volunteer the R rhythm warning (single passage; condition for raising R not met)
expectations.evidence: No rhythm/repetition (R) warning is raised as a finding. The only R reference is R.1 ('别把钩子用成反射动作'), cited to soften the ask and support the newsletter-needn't-always-hook point — not surfaced as a rhythm-across-passages problem, which is the condition being guarded against.

expectations.text: The feedback includes at least one specific, reasoned positive observation rather than generic praise
expectations.evidence: Two specific, reasoned positives: '"银色的珠帘""有时候直有时候斜"是被观察出来的、精确的画面，不是"下了很大的雨"这种概述' and '"分不清是蛙还是虫"是一个漂亮的、被感知到的事实级扰动……具体的、未解释的、真实的.' Both cite the exact text and give the reason — the target '声音太响太多，我分不清' as perceived fact is explicitly identified.

expectations.text: If the feedback offers a rewritten ending, it does NOT introduce a double-uncertainty, sympathy-fishing formulation such as "I don't even know how many people are reading this"
expectations.evidence: The offered rewrite is '感谢你还在听我念叨。\n雨停了，窗外那片声音还在，我还是分不清是蛙是虫。就这样吧，我们下周再见。' It affirms the reader is listening and carries only the single sound-uncertainty; no self-pitying double-uncertainty about the audience is introduced.

claims.claim: '分不清是蛙是虫' is a single, specific, perceived fact — a good disturbance, not an emotion word
claims.evidence: Draft line 35: '也可能是虫鸣，只是声音太响太多，我分不清。' This is a concrete perceptual fact left unidentified, correctly classified as a fact-level disturbance, not a named emotion.

claims.claim: The final sentence tells the reader how to feel ('更持久'/'更让我开心') rather than showing perception
claims.evidence: Draft line 37: '这种感觉比大雨更持久，比虫鸣更让我开心' — an explicit told feeling / conclusion, matching the Part 4 fail signal the feedback cites.

claims.claim: The strongest perception beat sits one sentence back at '声音太响太多，我分不清'
claims.evidence: That line (draft 35) is the last unexplained perceptual image before the told-feeling close; the feedback's recommendation to land on it is well grounded.

suggestions.assertion: The feedback does NOT volunteer the R rhythm warning
suggestions.reason: The output cites R.1 by name (to soften the ask). The assertion targets the R *rhythm* warning specifically; consider tightening the wording so a grader isn't tempted to fail on any mention of an R-prefixed note — distinguish 'raises the rhythm/repetition warning as a finding' from 'references R.1 as a softener'.

No assertion checks that the feedback keeps the deletion truly minimal (i.e. does not rewrite the whole vignette). The output happens to reorder+trim only the final paragraph, but a much heavier rewrite could still pass expectation 4 as long as the pivot line survives. An assertion bounding the edit size would make the 'deletion-first, minimal' claim more discriminating.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are well-targeted and discriminating for the core behavior (stop-at-first-failure, no scorecard, correct 4.2 diagnosis, no 4.1 false-positive on the pivot, newsletter awareness). Two minor tightening opportunities noted above.
